picks.rationale: Free prompt-driven synth that turns text descriptions into editable patches, with an optional local Ollama model. Producers can use it right away and it is fresh (Sep 24).
picks.excerpt: Free beta synth that builds editable patches from written descriptions, via a research-based database mode or an optional local AI model through Ollama that lets you keep refining the patch with text instructions.

picks.rationale: Suno Studio adds direct audio recording to the timeline, moving its AI DAW toward a hybrid human-plus-AI workflow. A primary-source feature release (Sep 23).
picks.excerpt: Suno Studio now lets you arm a track and record audio directly onto the timeline of its AI-assisted DAW.

picks.rationale: AI stem separation built into a live vocal pedal. It brings AI into hardware for live performers, a different angle from the software picks.
picks.excerpt: MOOER's VE200 is a compact stereo vocal multi-effects pedal for live performers with real-time processing and an AI StemLab stem-separation feature built in.

picks.rationale: Qobuz starts flagging AI-generated tracks in its catalog. This is a concrete platform labeling rollout that affects how AI-assisted releases are shown to listeners.
picks.excerpt: Qobuz is rolling out tags that flag AI-generated tracks in its catalog, saying musical discovery must remain guided by human choices.

picks.rationale: Voice-Swap joins DDEX to push consent and authorization metadata standards for AI vocals, which shapes how licensed AI voices move through production and distribution.
picks.excerpt: AI vocal platform Voice-Swap has joined DDEX and plans to contribute consent and authorization metadata standards as AI vocals become part of real production and commercial workflows.
